rationale: Reproduced against systemd 255.4 user manager output and the pinned Mycelium parser. systemctl show serializes argv with strv_join(..., " ") and does not escape an argument semicolon; the [^;]* capture therefore stops inside the allowed-signers path and omits the later --insecure-no-verify flag. The later bypass check misses that flag. This is a diagnostic false negative only: the pinned updater separately refuses the bypass whenever INVOCATION_ID is set or stdin is not a TTY. No unsigned root execution or security-boundary violation is established.
The sed capture extracts ports from local ss output for a liveness/status check. It does not enforce a trust boundary; expected port presence is checked separately with whole-line grep.
The UDP variant has the same local ss-to-port status role as the TCP candidate; same sink and no independent boundary guarantee.

The --repo-ref parser consumes the same truncated exec_all value produced by rank 1. The systemd replay consequently yields an empty ref, and the pinned script takes its explicit "--repo-ref present but its value could not be parsed" warning path. This is a downstream symptom of rank 1, not an independent contract.
The sed expression strips a local sing-box version banner for operator display; it does not gate or transform untrusted input.
Same local sing-box version-banner expression at a second status call site; duplicate display behavior.
The local Xray version banner is displayed for status only; no security decision consumes the capture.
The expression excludes systemd comment lines before template/deployed configuration comparison. Comments are inactive systemd syntax; the regex does not enforce an attacker-input boundary.
Trailing whitespace is trimmed before a configuration diff. This normalization does not determine whether a command or security flag reaches the effective unit.
Trailing spaces are removed from the captured ExecStart display before concatenation and checks. The independently ranked argv extraction remains unresolved.

The exact pinned verifier requires a 64-hex SHA256 record before invoking the platform checksum command. Its comments and release docs identify empty/truncated or HTTP error bodies as input and the integrity result as the sink; the contract is deliberately limited to the preflight and does not claim authenticity.
The awk/sed expression extracts a usage block from the script header for help output; this is documentation rendering, not a security boundary.
The expression filters loopback addresses from a read-only listener display. It does not configure listeners, authorize traffic, or control an enforcement decision.
The expression removes empty lines from a read-only systemd configuration listing; no separate security guarantee depends on the regex.
The expression removes empty records from a diagnostic ExecStart listing; no independent contract-backed security property is present.
